name: GERMANY

flag.title: Flag of Germany
flag.note: Three equal bands: black, red, gold

lead: Germany is in the middle of Europe. It has dark fairy-tale forests, snowy Alps and busy cities. Germans invented the printing press, the car and the Christmas tree. About 84 million people live here, the most in Europe.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Germany has flat, windy coasts in the north and rolling farms in the middle. The south has the jagged Bavarian Alps. The Zugspitze reaches 2,962 metres.
Forests cover nearly a third of Germany. The Black Forest is so dark and thick that it inspired the Brothers Grimm fairy tales. Rivers like the Rhine and Elbe pass castle-topped hills.
animals: Wild boar are bristly pigs with tusks. They snuffle through forest leaves for acorns. There are so many that some wander into Berlin's suburbs at night.
Every spring, white storks fly home from Africa to the same rooftop nest. Germans think they bring luck. Red squirrels with ear tufts still dart through pine trees.
culture: Germany has over 1,300 kinds of bread, more than any other country. UNESCO lists German bread-making as cultural heritage. A thick dark rye loaf often arrives first at lunch.
Bach, Beethoven and Brahms were all German. Germany has over 80 opera houses, the most in the world. Christmas markets began here about 500 years ago.
history: For centuries, Germany was many small kingdoms and free cities. It became one nation in 1871. After World War II, it split into West and East Germany. The Berlin Wall divided them.
In 1989, the wall came tumbling down. East and West joined again in 1990. Today Germany is Europe's biggest economy.
wows: Hamburg has over 2,300 bridges, more than Venice, Amsterdam and London combined.
Hans Riegel invented the gummy bear in Bonn in 1922.
Some Autobahn sections have no speed limit, which no other big motorway network allows.
Gutenberg printed Europe's first book with movable type around 1450.
Czechs drink more beer per person than Germans, who rank only seventh.
Germans eat over 800 million currywurst a year, 70 million in Berlin.
Germany has 16 states, each with its own parliament and police.

myths.fact: Lederhosen are Bavarian folk dress, worn mostly at festivals. In Berlin, people wear jeans.
Oktoberfest starts in September and ends in early October.
